skill.name: zentao-task-planner
skill.description: Plan ZenTao work schedules and run guided ZenTao task operations for creation, listing, completion, repair, and closure.
skill.summary: Plan and manage ZenTao tasks with preview-first scripts.
skill.author: AriesYB

security_audit.summary: The skill legitimately manages ZenTao tasks, but it handles local credentials, performs authenticated network requests, and can mutate project records. Many static hits are false positives from Markdown backticks, user-agent strings, and normal ID parsing. No prompt injection evidence was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: ZenTao password is sent through request query parameters.
remediation.suggestion: Send credentials in the request body or an approved authentication flow, and avoid logging full login URLs.

remediation.issue: The skill reads .env files containing ZenTao credentials.
remediation.suggestion: Document strict file permissions, support secret managers where possible, and avoid storing task plans beside credential files.

remediation.issue: Scripts can create, finish, repair, and close ZenTao tasks.
remediation.suggestion: Keep dry-run as the default and require explicit confirmation that includes task counts, IDs, and target dates.

remediation.issue: Error handling can print full authenticated server responses.
remediation.suggestion: Replace full response debug output with redacted status, endpoint, and parse-error details.

remediation.issue: Network target comes from user-provided configuration.
remediation.suggestion: Require HTTPS by default, validate the base URL, and warn before connecting to non-production or unknown hosts.

semantic_findings.title: Credentials Sent in Login Query Parameters
semantic_findings.description: The ZenTao login posts account and password through request parameters, which places credentials in the URL query string. Logs and proxies may retain those values.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The login method calls requests.post with params containing account and password. In requests, params are encoded into the URL query string.

semantic_findings.title: Business System State Changes
semantic_findings.description: The skill can create, finish, repair, and close ZenTao tasks after preview. If execution is approved incorrectly, it can alter project records.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The docs and code show preview defaults plus explicit execution paths for task creation, completion, repair, and closure. This is intended functionality but has business impact.

semantic_findings.title: Authenticated Response Debug Output
semantic_findings.description: On JSON parsing failure, the client prints the full response text. Authenticated ZenTao responses may contain project, user, or task details.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The debug print is on an error path, so exposure depends on failures and terminal logging. The response is authenticated content, so the risk is plausible.

content.value_statement: ZenTao planning often needs dates, task types, and careful confirmation. This skill drafts task plans and runs preview-first ZenTao operations.
actual_capabilities: Drafts tab-separated ZenTao task plans from user requirements and working dates.
Looks up current or next continuous workdays for scheduling.
Lists ZenTao task views with summary or TSV output.
Validates task tables, user mappings, stories, and task types before creation.
Previews and executes task creation only when requested.
Previews and executes task completion, date repair, and closure workflows.
limitations: Requires a reachable ZenTao instance and valid ZenTao credentials.
Writes to ZenTao only through the included scripts and documented fields.
Task type mapping can fall back to a static list when ZenTao parsing fails.
Date planning depends on user confirmation and available working-day data.

use_cases.title: Weekly Task Planning
use_cases.description: Convert requirements and working days into a structured task plan before any ZenTao write action.

use_cases.title: Team Task Setup
use_cases.description: Validate assignees, stories, and task types, then preview batch task creation for a confirmed plan.

use_cases.title: Task Cleanup and Corrections
use_cases.description: Preview task completion, completion-date repair, and closure for finished work records.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Next Workdays
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan my ZenTao tasks for next week. Ask for my name, requirement ID, and missing details before drafting the table.

prompt_templates.title: Preview Task Creation
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this confirmed task plan to preview ZenTao task creation. Do not execute creation until I approve the preview.

prompt_templates.title: Review Active Tasks
prompt_templates.prompt: List my active ZenTao tasks as a concise summary. Highlight deadlines, remaining hours, and tasks that may need updates.

prompt_templates.title: Repair and Close Tasks
prompt_templates.prompt: Preview repairs for task completion dates, then preview closing finished tasks. Execute only after I confirm each preview.

output_examples.input: I need a next-week plan for requirement 103615 and my name is Zhang San.
output_examples.output: The skill asks for missing scope details, checks working dates, and returns a tab-separated planning table.

output_examples.input: Create ZenTao tasks from this confirmed table.
output_examples.output: It validates users, task types, and stories, then shows a creation preview before any write action.
It lists matching tasks and expected consumed hours, then waits for explicit approval before completion.

best_practices: Run every ZenTao write workflow in preview mode before using execution mode.
Store credentials outside shared folders and restrict file permissions.
Confirm task IDs, assignees, dates, and estimated hours before approving writes.
anti_patterns: Do not run execution mode from an unreviewed task table.
Do not paste production credentials into chat prompts or task plans.
Do not assume dates when the user has not confirmed the work period.

faq.question: Does this skill create tasks automatically?
faq.answer: It previews task creation by default. Actual creation requires the documented execution flag after user approval.

faq.question: What credentials does it need?
faq.answer: It needs ZenTao base URL, account, password, and sometimes a display name in environment variables.

faq.question: Can it list existing ZenTao tasks?
faq.answer: Yes. It can list active, assigned, finished, or closed task views with JSON or TSV output.

faq.question: Can it handle custom task types?
faq.answer: It tries to parse task types from ZenTao. It falls back to an included static mapping if parsing fails.

faq.question: Does it support holiday-aware planning?
faq.answer: Yes. It can use the Chinese calendar package and falls back to weekday-only logic when unavailable.

faq.question: Is it safe for shared workstations?
faq.answer: Use caution. The skill reads local environment files and can perform authenticated ZenTao changes after approval.
